newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki shrugs off Nokia dip, forestries shine.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki shrugs off Nokia dip, forestries shine.

text.p: * Shares edge higher in thin summer trade despite a softer start by Nokia, and seen steady, brokers say. Partek up in million-share in-house deal by Carnegie. Forestries shine.
Shares opened flat and then edged upward on Friday, shrugging off a softer start for Nokia with forestries outperforming and with the overall trend seen flat, brokers said.

"I think we'll stay at about these levels (on the main indices)," today, one broker said with the FOX index up about 0.2 percent, adding that most of the 230 million markka trade was concentrated in just a few shares.
Nokia pared early losses to trade 1.00 markka lower at 417.00 in modest volume, three markka above its U.S. close.
Forestries stood out, with the subindex up 1.55 percent.
UPM-Kymmene hit a 135.50 life-high and later stood at 134.50, up 1.40, while Enso advanced 1.80 markka to its highest ever 51.00 in solid 60 million markka trade.
Brokers said forestries continued to draw strength from bullishness towards paper-makers in the United States, where the S&P paper stocks subindex rose 2.54 percent on Thursday.
Partek traded up 0.50 markka at 99.50 and was the most traded share after Carnegie crossed a one million share deal inhouse at 100.00 per share.
